issues.description: The problem specification and the solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(): void (see UML and solution), but the template Stock class defines the method as clearInventory(). This name mismatch is structural and will confuse students (and break tests) because the expected method name in the spec/solution does not exist in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() to match the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, add a public emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory() so both names are supported (preserves backward compatibility and aligns with the UML/spec).

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template implementation provides a method named clearInventory(). This mismatch can confuse students when they try to locate or implement the required method, since the template and the specification use different identifiers for the same conceptual operation (clearing the stock).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier across artifacts: rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (and update any callers), or alternatively update the problem statement to require clearInventory(). Prefer making the template match the problem statement and solution by using emptyStock().
